proposals.title: Open a running story in the side panel, its steps opening their tasks
proposals.prompt:
Clicking a story card in Current sprint, including one that is running, opens
the story in Planning's side panel, the way any other card opens, as
spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.stories says. Clicking it no longer jumps
to its task in the Tasks tab. This replaces "clicking it opens its task in the
Tasks tab" in spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint. The card stays
highlighted with the accent line while it is open. Clicking it again, Escape,
or the panel's close button closes it. Enter on the focused card does the same,
as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.keyboard says.

The story is still read-only once it has been sent. Its title, prompt,
parameters, and citations are shown but can't be edited. It has no Add step and
no step reordering, since "its steps, sent or still to come, read as they were
sent" (spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.steps). The panel lists all its
steps, step 1 (its own prompt) first, as rows drawn as
spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.parts draws them. Each row shows its
number, its mode pill, the first line of its prompt, and its own live status,
the way the card's step lines and a running chain's rows in the Tasks tab show
it (Queued, Running with its time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, Held for review,
Next, Waiting). The rows update as the chain runs.

Clicking a step row opens that step's task in the Tasks tab, as
spec/ui/components/right-sidebar/tasks/index.pi#TasksTab.rows opens a chain's
step. A story with no further steps has one row, step 1, which opens its task
the same way. A step not yet sent has no task to open, so its row isn't
clickable, and its tooltip says it hasn't been sent yet.

The spec has nothing yet on a sent story's panel showing live step statuses or
on step rows opening their tasks, so that part is new. Write it into
spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint and
spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.steps first, then change the code to match.

spec.note: what clicking a Current sprint card does now, which this replaces
spec.quote: clicking it opens its task in the Tasks tab; it can't be moved or edited there

spec.note: clicking a card opens the story in the side panel, and the open card stays highlighted
spec.quote: it opens the story in the side panel, docked at the board's right

spec.note: how an open story lists its steps, and how a sent story's steps read
spec.quote: A story sent can't be given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they were sent

spec.note: the side panel is where everything opens
spec.quote: The side panel is the one place anything opens

spec.note: the row part used for steps in an open story
spec.quote: A row: 36 pixels tall, for steps in an open story and for findings

spec.note: Enter on a focused card, which should do the same as a click
spec.quote: Enter opens or closes the focused story

spec.note: what opening a chain or one of its steps shows in the Tasks tab
spec.quote: Clicking the chain's row, or any of its steps, opens the chain

spec.note: an open story in the side panel showing each sent step's live status and opening that step's task when clicked

proposals.title: Settle how a sent story's panel reads
proposals.prompt:
Update spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.sprint and
spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.steps to match what the code now does
when a Current sprint story is opened in the side panel. Cover which of its
fields show read-only, what each step row's status reads and how it updates,
what clicking a sent step does versus one not yet sent, and where focus and
the Tasks tab end up. If the code changed how the Tasks tab opens a step, make
spec/ui/components/right-sidebar/tasks/index.pi#TasksTab.rows agree with it.

spec.note: what clicking a Current sprint card does
spec.quote: A story in Current sprint keeps its place

spec.note: how a sent story's steps are listed in the open story
spec.quote: An open story lists all its steps this way

spec.note: opening a step's task from Planning
spec.quote: Clicking the chain's row, or any of its steps, opens the chain
